review_notes: I read the whole file and checked how its simp lemmas relate to the parent `Lp`/`MemLp.toLp` API. I grepped for uses of the `toLp_*` lemmas across Mathlib. I found no loops or competing rules. The only simp-interface gap I found is the `toLp`/`toSimpleFunc` round trip. This file's own proof of `norm_toSimpleFunc` passes `toLp_toSimpleFunc` to simp by hand, and the Bochner file only uses `toSimpleFunc_toLp` via explicit `rw`/term. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether the suggested attribute would interact badly with other simp sets. I only report the one finding because the rest is not justified without more evidence. Most other rfl-lemmas here are deliberately non-simp, and I did not check their downstream effects.

findings.excerpt:
theorem toLp_toSimpleFunc (f : Lp.simpleFunc E p μ) :
    toLp (toSimpleFunc f) (simpleFunc.memLp f) = f :=
findings.problem: This is the round-trip normalization lemma: `toLp (toSimpleFunc f) _` rewrites to `f`. It is a directed equation that shrinks the term and has an unambiguous orientation, and the proof argument is irrelevant to matching. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. The file itself has to supply it by hand in `simpa [toLp_toSimpleFunc] using norm_toLp ...` in `norm_toSimpleFunc`. The parallel root lemma `MemLp.toLp_zero` is `@[simp]`, while the simpleFunc analogue `toLp_zero` (line 490) is not.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `toLp_toSimpleFunc` with `@[simp]`, so simp collapses `toLp (toSimpleFunc f) _` to `f`. The `simpa [toLp_toSimpleFunc]` call in `norm_toSimpleFunc` then needs no explicit lemma. Optionally also tag `SimpleFunc.toLp_zero` (`toLp 0 MemLp.zero = 0`) as `@[simp]`, matching the root `MemLp.toLp_zero`, which is `@[simp]`.
findings.benefit: Users of `Lp.simpleFunc` would get the canonical cancellation of `toLp`/`toSimpleFunc` from plain `simp`, as they do for `MemLp.toLp`, instead of passing the lemma by hand each time.
